tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Plastic Kits
tips.text: To strip old paint from plastic kits, use a chemical paint stripper like Citadel's 'Dettol' or Mr. Hobby's 'Mr. Thin'. Apply a thin layer with a brush, wait 10-15 minutes, then gently scrape off with a plastic scraper. For stubborn paint, soak the part in a jar with stripper for 24 hours, then scrub with a toothbrush.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Broken photo-etched parts can be repaired using CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue. Align the parts under magnification, apply a small drop of CA glue on the join, and hold together for 30 seconds. Use tweezers to apply gentle pressure. Once set, paint over the join with Vallejo Model Color to conceal.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog an airbrush, disassemble it and soak the nozzle, needle, and cap in Vallejo Airbrush Cleaner for 15 minutes. Use a soft brush to scrub gently, then reassemble and test-spray with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. If still clogged, use a needle-cleaning kit like Iwata's 'Eclipse' to remove dried paint from the needle.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Plastic Parts
tips.text: Warped plastic parts can be repaired using hot water. Immerse the warped part in hot (not boiling) water for 5 minutes, then carefully bend it back into shape using tweezers. Lay it flat to dry, keeping the warped side down. For thicker parts, use a heat gun (like Tamiya's) to soften the plastic, then mold it back into shape.

tips.title: Fixing Paint Reactions/Bubbling
tips.text: Paint reactions or bubbling can be caused by contamination or high humidity. To fix, sand the affected area lightly with fine sandpaper, wipe clean with alcohol, and apply a retouching paint like Vallejo's 'Mecha Color' using a fine brush. Seal with a gloss coat, then apply flat coat once fully dry.
